claims: The Solicitor General of the United States is often called the "tenth justice".
The Solicitor General of the United States is the Department of Justice official responsible for representing the federal government's interests before the Supreme Court.
The U.S. Solicitor General is appointed by the President.
The U.S. Solicitor General determines which cases the government appeals.
The U.S. Solicitor General files amicus briefs.
The U.S. Solicitor General supervises all litigation in the U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of the United States.
The U.S. Solicitor General conducts all litigation in the U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of the United States.
The U.S. Solicitor General determines whether the government will appeal cases from lower federal and state courts.
The U.S. Solicitor General determines to what extent the government will appeal cases from lower federal and state courts.
The U.S. Solicitor General files briefs in cases where the government is not a direct party but has an interest.
The U.S. Solicitor General decides when the United States should intervene to defend the constitutionality of Acts of Congress.
The Office of the Solicitor General was created by Congress in 1870.
D. John Sauer is serving as the 49th U.S. Solicitor General as of April 2025.
D. John Sauer represented the Trump administration in major litigation regarding presidential immunity.
Studies show an agreement rate of over 70% for the Solicitor General in cases where they weigh in.
Thurgood Marshall was a past U.S. Solicitor General.
Robert Bork was a past U.S. Solicitor General.
Kenneth Starr was a past U.S. Solicitor General.
Elena Kagan was a past U.S. Solicitor General.
Many states have a Solicitor General who handles appellate litigation for that state's Attorney General.
The District of Columbia has a Solicitor General.
